item.description: When Randy Cassingham returned to his US$379,000 cabin aboard the Villa Vie Odyssey in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, ship security had to break a seal on the door. He retrieved his medication and some clothes, but had to leave behind several pairs of new shoes and a US$1,500 desk chair he had bought for an office he rented aboard the ship. He and his wife, Kit, had even bought new pillows for a bed they thought they would be sleeping in for years to come. “We got two years of use out of our cabin …...

item.description: The local elections in Taiwan on Saturday will offer Beijing a window into shifting public sentiment and the island’s political trajectory ahead of its 2028 general poll, with the results potentially affecting city-level cross-strait exchanges, according to analysts. The “nine-in-one” elections – to decide the island’s mayors, county magistrates and thousands of grass-roots officials – are widely viewed as a midterm test for Taiwan’s leader William Lai Ching-te, who took office in May 2024. But...

item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Vladimir Putin to “pull back all military aggression” against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone towards the Russian leader he called his friend just last week. Trump said he had made the request to Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow’s grinding war in Ukraine. Trump’s comments come a day after he hosted Nato chief Mark Rutte in Florida, after which the two leaders issued a...

item.dc:creator: Lawrence Chung
item.description: Taiwan’s growing demand for electricity to sustain its semiconductor and AI industries has thrust a nuclear power referendum into the spotlight in Saturday’s local elections. The vote could also offer Taiwanese leader William Lai Ching-te a way out of a political dilemma as his administration explored the possibility of reviving nuclear power despite decades of opposition from his ruling Democratic Progressive Party, analysts said. Taiwan became nuclear-free in May last year when its final...
item.title: Will Taiwan’s referendum bring back nuclear power as chips and AI strain the grid?

item.author: Denise Tsang
item.dc:creator: Denise Tsang
item.description: A high-speed passenger ferry has collided with a floating dry dock off the waters of Tsing Yi oil depot and left 22 people injured, with four in serious condition, according to Hong Kong police. The force said on Friday that it received a report at 9.25am. Fifteen ambulances arrived at the scene, with emergency responders conducting rescue operations. A source said the ferry’s captain found the helm malfunctioning, lost control of the boat and crashed into the floating dry dock. Forty passengers...

item.author: Alice Yan
item.dc:creator: Alice Yan
item.description: A job applicant in China discovered that her interview had been cancelled after she refused to buy a drink for the company’s human resources manager. The incident, shared by a woman surnamed Wang, has attracted significant attention online. Her post has been viewed more than 70 million times across several Chinese social media platforms, the Yangtze Evening News reported. Wang, who lives in Kunshan, in eastern China’s Jiangsu province, said she found a job listing on the recruitment platform...
item.title: Chinese job applicant claims HR staffer cancelled interview after she refused to buy drink

item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: A drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians working on an air defence system on Thursday, marking the first fatal strike in the Gulf state for months. Both Italy and Kuwait confirmed the deaths, blaming the attack on Iran. But Tehran’s foreign minister Abbas Araghchi insisted in calls to his Kuwaiti and Italian counterparts that it was not behind the deadly strike. Iran has in the last week ratcheted up attacks on Kuwait and Gulf neighbour Bahrain while it continues to fight the...
item.title: Iran denies role in drone attack that killed Italians in Kuwait

item.author: Alice Li,Mia Nurmamat
item.dc:creator: Alice Li,Mia Nurmamat
item.description: Skiing has long been considered an expensive sport in China, with the industry heavily reliant on imported specialised equipment and machinery for resorts. But domestic manufacturers are beginning to reshape the market by offering cheaper alternatives while also expanding overseas. The shift is already visible at indoor ski centres in Shenzhen, where locally made equipment is increasingly being used for ski lessons and rental services. “Domestic equipment has improved rapidly and is particularly...
item.title: Skiing in China was once a luxury. Local manufacturers are slashing costs

item.dc:creator: Liu Zhen

item.title: Is the US reviving Subic Bay in the Philippines as an ‘unbranded military base’?

item.description: A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Thursday, as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history. item.author: Dana Humaid Al Marzooqi
item.dc:creator: Dana Humaid Al Marzooqi
item.description: Artificial intelligence is giving offenders new ways to exploit children. Images of real children can be AI-manipulated into sexual abuse material, while chatbots allow users to rehearse abusive encounters and, in some cases, obtain guidance on grooming. These systems can also help offenders construct convincing false identities and tailor messages to gain a young person’s trust, raising the prospect of grooming more children with less time and effort. The pace of that change is visible. The...
item.title: AI is changing child exploitation. Our response must change too

item.dc:creator: Emily Hung
item.description: Hong Kong’s Immigration Department has arrested a woman and her boyfriend for allegedly altering a travel document unlawfully after she took to social media to complain about a “manufacturing defect” in her passport that caused Japan’s authorities to deny her entry. The couple, who are aged between 27 and 34, were arrested on Thursday night from a public housing estate in Lam Tin on suspicion of unlawful alteration of a travel document and misleading the immigration service. item.description: After spending most of her life in the United States, leading neuroscientist Cao Ying – better known as Doris Tsao – has decided to leave California’s prestigious UC Berkeley at the peak of her scientific career for a new Chinese research university that has not yet been built. Unlike most Chinese scientists who moved to the United States as adults, often not until their PhD, Tsao received an American-style education from an early age after emigrating to the US aged four. item.description:
Just over a year ago, Carlo Ople was making YouTube videos about his two obsessions – trainers and action figures. These days, the 44-year-old former marketing executive uses the same channel to dissect national budgets and political issues, swearing profusely along the way. item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron set an end-of-year deadline for an agreement on the European Union’s next seven-year budget after the continent’s leaders ruled out any chances for a deal to be reached at their summit on Thursday. The 2028-2034 budget – a statement on broader EU ambitions – is small, compared to national budgets, and it is financed mostly by the 27 member countries based on the size of their economies. It is likely to amount to between 1 per cent and 1.2 per cent of the EU’s...
item.title: EU leaders unable to agree on budget after over 12 hours of talks: ‘zero results’

item.description: Lunch is likely to remain on the menu for Hong Kong stock brokers, as the city’s bourse operator leans towards extending trading hours at either end of the day while keeping the market’s traditional mid-day break intact, according to multiple sources. item.description: A man who went on the rampage armed with a knife on a London-bound train was on Thursday found guilty of the attempted murder of 14 people. A jury found Anthony Williams, 33, guilty of all 10 counts of attempted murder on the train involving passengers and an on-board staff member, as well as earlier incidents in London and another UK town in which four others were injured. item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Spain’s Pablo Hernandez de Cos will be the next head of the European Central Bank, taking over from Christine Lagarde, diplomats said on Thursday. His nomination comes at a time of tension on European bond markets and before a series of high-stakes elections in Europe next year, including in France. Hernandez de Cos, 55, has been head of the Swiss-based Bank for International Settlements (BIS) since last year, and previously led the Bank of Spain from 2018 to 2024. The ECB is the central bank...

item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Thursday accused his Commerce Department of purposely issuing incorrect economic growth figures before the midterm elections and said he wants to launch an investigation. Trump has repeatedly sought to undermine trust in economic data that fails to match his claims of a historic boom, a pattern that threatens the credibility of figures needed by businesses, financial markets and consumers when making investments. item.dc:creator: Chao Kong
item.description: More than half of Americans believe China has already overtaken or will eventually surpass the United States in technology, economic strength and even military power, according to a study based on US public opinion data. The proportions reached 68.8 per cent in technology, 65.2 per cent in economic strength and 58.3 per cent in military power. item.dc:creator: Biman Mukherji

Speaking at the annual convention of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry last week, Modi said his government had cut the base corporate tax rate from 30 per cent in the 2014–15 financial year to 22 per cent in late 2019. item.author: dpa
item.dc:creator: dpa
item.description: A court in western Germany ordered the archdiocese of Cologne on Thursday to pay a woman €550,000 (US$600,000) in damages for sexual abuse. It is the highest amount a German court has ever awarded to a victim of abuse in the Catholic Church. The previous highest award was €300,000, according to the Higher Regional Court of Cologne. The €550,000 award is to be offset by €360,000 that the Catholic Church’s Independent Commission for Recognition Payments has already paid to the claimant. The woman...

item.author: Caroline Lin,Eve Qiao
item.dc:creator: Caroline Lin,Eve Qiao
item.description: China has cracked down on the smuggling of blood samples from pregnant women, highlighting what authorities describe as a threat to national biosecurity. State broadcaster CCTV reported on Wednesday that Shenzhen Customs anti-smuggling officers had dismantled an underground network that illegally collected and transported the blood out of mainland China. The samples were used for fetal sex determination, a practice banned on the mainland for non-medical purposes. Following a nearly year-long...

item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Net migration to the UK fell to 77,000 for the year to June, the lowest annual figure since 1997 excluding the Covid years, statistics showed on Thursday. The net migration figures – the difference between the numbers of people arriving in and leaving Britain – are a boost for the UK’s centre-left Labour government, which has been under pressure from the hard right anti-immigration Reform UK party on the issue. However, some economists have questioned whether low net migration is compatible with...

item.author: SCMP’s Asia desk
item.dc:creator: SCMP’s Asia desk
item.description: A Singaporean trainee surgeon who secretly filmed hundreds of his female colleagues in Australian hospitals was remanded on Thursday. Ryan Cho, 29, will be sentenced on February 12 after he pleaded guilty to recording 874 women at three major Melbourne hospitals and shared houses, according to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation. The court heard that Cho used a phone hidden in a mesh bag to spy on women, meticulously cataloguing and storing the footage on his laptop. To get his victims to...

item.dc:creator: Fiona Sun

Legislators Jonathan Leung Chun and Bill Tang Ka-piu, who sit on the institution’s governing council, said on Thursday that much of the ordinance’s content had failed to keep pace with current societal and legislative changes, necessitating the amendments. item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Vietnam must explain how three pro-democracy activists ended up in detention facing terrorism charges after being allegedly abducted from neighbouring Cambodia, United Nations experts said on Thursday. Vietnam permits little to no dissent within its borders and critics say its security apparatus stretches abroad, with wanted dissidents previously abducted in Thailand and Germany. The authorities in Hanoi confirmed in September they had arrested three men – an Australian, a Norwegian and a...

item.author: Gabriel Dominguez
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Dominguez
item.description: Tokyo is planning to introduce a new long-range anti-ship missile that could be launched from a broader range of vessels, according to Japanese media reports, potentially complicating Chinese military planning in a conflict. The proposed capability could allow Japan to equip vessels that traditionally do not carry anti-ship missiles, according to defence experts. For much of the past four decades, China’s paramount goal was integration. It sought access to markets, technology, investment and institutions to fuel its modernisation and development.
